body_html:
How it works

A linear equation in two variables can be written as ax + by + c = 0, where a and b are not both 0.

A solution is a pair (x, y) that makes the equation true. A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions: choose any x and work out y.

On the x-axis y = 0; on the y-axis x = 0. Even x = 3 is an equation in two variables: 1·x + 0·y − 3 = 0.

Example

Write 2x = −5y in the form ax + by + c = 0.

2x + 5y = 0

Answer: a = 2, b = 5, c = 0

Example

Find k if x = 2, y = 1 is a solution of 2x + 3y = k.

2(2) + 3(1)

Answer: k = 7

Common mistakes

  • Keeping the sign of c when moving it from the right-hand side. Its sign changes.
  • Swapping x and y when checking a pair (x, y).
  • Saying a linear equation in two variables has one solution. It has infinitely many.

faq.q: What is a linear equation in two variables?
faq.a: An equation that can be written as ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero.

faq.q: How many solutions does a linear equation in two variables have?
faq.a: Infinitely many. Every point on its straight-line graph is a solution.

faq.q: How do I check whether a pair is a solution?
faq.a: Substitute the values of x and y. If both sides are equal, the pair is a solution.

items.q: Write 3x = 2y − 4 in the form ax + by + c = 0. What are a, b and c?
